# Appendix A3: Using PyCharm Community {#sec-appendix-a3 .unnumbered}

This appendix assumes you've completed [Part 0](../chapters/chapter_00.qmd) —
Python installed, `.venv` created and active, packages installed via
`pip install -r requirements.txt`. Everything below is specific to
working with this book's code in PyCharm Community Edition (free).

## Install PyCharm Community

Download it from
[jetbrains.com/pycharm/download](https://www.jetbrains.com/pycharm/download/)
— choose the **Community** edition, not Professional.

## Open the project folder

`File > Open...` and select the `llm-ft-drilling-completions-book`
folder you cloned in Part 0.

## Point PyCharm at your virtual environment

`File > Settings` (Windows/Linux) or `PyCharm > Settings` (macOS) >
**Project: llm-ft-drilling-completions-book > Python Interpreter** > gear
icon > **Add** > **Existing environment**, and browse to the `.venv`
folder created in Part 0 (`.venv/bin/python` on macOS/Linux,
`.venv\Scripts\python.exe` on Windows).

**Expected result:** the interpreter dropdown at the bottom of the
Settings page shows your `.venv` path.

## Run a chapter script

Right-click `book/code/chapter_01/load_local_model.py` in the Project
panel and choose **Run 'load_local_model'**. Output appears in the Run
panel at the bottom.

## Run the tests

Right-click the `book/tests` folder and choose **Run 'pytest in
tests'**. PyCharm shows a tree of passing/failing tests.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause |
|---|---|
| Interpreter list doesn't show `.venv` | Confirm Part 0's virtual environment was actually created inside the project folder, not elsewhere. |
| Red underlines on valid imports | PyCharm hasn't finished indexing, or the wrong interpreter is selected — check the bottom-right corner of the window. |
